interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into both pre-Pearl Harbor economic intelligence and wartime State Department information management. The 1941 documents illustrate how commercial war-risk insurance quotations on the Calcutta–New York route served as intelligence indicators, suggesting to American analysts that Japanese underwriters did not anticipate imminent British naval seizures of Japanese bottoms months before the Pacific War began. In addition, the 1944 correspondence shows how the State Department handled public inquiries by providing historical and statistical data from the Japan Year Book while strictly enforcing disclaimers to ensure official U.S. government endorsement was not attached to secondary economic figures.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.5062) contains State Department correspondence and internal memoranda from April 1941 and April 1944 concerning Japanese marine and war-risk insurance. The earlier 1941 documents comprise an intelligence memorandum and transmittal slip originating from Philadelphia underwriter J. Brooks B. Parker and processed by Edward L. Reed and Cabot Coville, reporting that Japanese underwriters offered lower rates than American underwriters for cargo shipped in Japanese bottoms from Calcutta to New York via Kobe including British seizure risk, indicating Japanese confidence that Britain would not detain their vessels. The 1944 records center on an inquiry from William E. Healy, Associate Editor of the Pacific Northwest Underwriter, addressed to former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Japanese merchant marine insurance; this prompted an internal research memorandum compiled from the Japan Year Book by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs detailing the history, capitalization, and pre-war statistics of Japanese and foreign marine insurance companies, which Grew subsequently forwarded to Healy with attribution guidelines.

subfiles.about: Inquiry from an insurance journal editor asking Joseph C. Grew for information regarding the organization and handling of Japanese merchant marine insurance.
subfiles.summary: William E. Healy, Associate Editor of the Pacific Northwest Underwriter, writes to Special Assistant Joseph C. Grew expressing appreciation for Grew's recent article in the National Geographic. Healy asks whether Japan's merchant marine insurance was handled by the government, private domestic companies, or foreign underwriters. He requests basic background information on the subject to serve as the foundation for an upcoming article.
subfiles.title: Letter from William E. Healy to Joseph C. Grew requesting information on Japanese merchant marine insurance

subfiles.about: State Department letter furnishing historical and statistical data on Japanese marine insurance companies based on the Japan Year Book.
subfiles.summary: Joseph C. Grew replies to William E. Healy's request, summarizing the development of marine insurance in Japan since its inception in Tokyo in January 1879 by Eiichi Shibusawa and Yataro Iwasaki. The letter outlines 1938–1939 fiscal data, observing that while roughly 20 domestic companies were active, approximately 12 firms conducted the bulk of the business. Grew notes the pre-war operations and subsequent decline of foreign insurance firms between 1938 and 1941 due to strict government regulations and exchange difficulties, and specifies that published citations must reference the 1940–1941 Japan Year Book rather than the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to William E. Healy regarding Japanese marine insurance

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum requesting the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to draft a reply to William E. Healy's inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Joseph C. Grew transmits William E. Healy's letter to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. He requests that the division check for available information concerning Japanese marine insurance and draft an appropriate response to Healy. The memorandum carries routing and receipt stamps from the Office of Far Eastern Affairs and the Division of Communications and Records.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Joseph C. Grew to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs requesting draft reply

subfiles.about: Departmental research memorandum outlining historical and statistical information on Japanese marine insurance compiled from the Japan Year Book.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs provides Joseph C. Grew with detailed data on Japanese marine insurance taken from the Japan Year Book. The memorandum traces the industry's founding in 1879 by Eiichi Shibusawa and Yataro Iwasaki of Mitsubishi with 650,000 yen capital, summarizes premium, expense, and contract figures for 1938–1939, and details foreign company operations in 1937–1938. It also explains that mounting shipping difficulties and stricter Japanese regulations caused a marked decline in foreign insurance business between 1938 and 1941.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Joseph C. Grew on Japanese marine insurance

subfiles.about: Memorandum detailing Japanese commercial marine and war-risk insurance rates on shipments from Calcutta to New York via Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Cabot Coville of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs reports on information received from Philadelphia insurance broker J. Brooks B. Parker regarding a Japanese insurance company's offer to cover cargo valued at $125,000 on Japanese bottoms from Calcutta to New York via Kobe. The Japanese insurer offered a rate of 3 percent covering normal and war risks including British seizure, whereas the prevailing American rate excluding British seizure was 3.5 percent. The memo highlights Parker's deduction that Japanese underwriters did not expect immediate difficulties or seizures from British authorities, and notes that Edward L. Reed is handling personal acknowledgment.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Cabot Coville regarding Japanese war-risk insurance rates between Calcutta and New York

subfiles.about: Transmittal slip from the Division of Controls referring J. Brooks B. Parker's letter to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Edward L. Reed of the Division of Controls forwards J. Brooks B. Parker's communication to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs for attention. Reed notes that the author is personally and favorably known to him.
subfiles.title: Routing slip from Edward L. Reed to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs
